tip: lite grann is a fixed phrase meaning a tiny bit; grann here is not the word for neighbor.
For body parts Swedish uses the definite form, so bröt armen means broke his arm, not bröt sin arm.
Start with a time word like Imorgon and the verb är comes before the subject det.
hem means toward home for motion; being located at home is hemma.
vuxit is the irregular supine of växa (to grow), the form used after har.
After är a predicate adjective adds -a for a plural subject: vi är glada.
sett is the irregular supine of se (to see), the form used after har.
vunnit is the supine of vinna; strong verbs shift the i to u here.
Clock times use klockan: landar klockan tre means lands at three.
inga is the plural of ingen: inga direktflyg means no direct flights.
A definite adjective needs both a front word and a noun ending: det lilla barnet.
hela is followed by a definite noun with no extra article: hela dagen, the whole day.
skrivit is the supine of skriva (to write), the form used after har.
mitt is the my form for ett-words: mitt lösenord; en-words take min instead.
sin means one's own and refers back to the subject: sin plånbok is her own wallet.
att before a verb marks the infinitive, like English to: att flytta means to move.
tänka pairs with på for about: tänkt på saken means thought about the matter.
hört talas om is a set phrase meaning to have heard about something.
When vem is the subject of an embedded clause it takes som: vem som hade ringt.
After med a means of transport drops its article: med bil means by car.
Past unreal conditions use hade plus the supine in both halves: hade vetat, hade kommit.
Innan means before and opens a time clause: Innan du går, before you leave.
Nu när means now that, setting up a current reason: Nu när du är här.
bestämma sig för means decide on, needing the reflexive oss and för: bestämt oss för.
The -s ending can mean each other: setts means seen one another, from se.
bästa is the irregular superlative of bra and god: den bästa filmen, the best film.
en-words ending in -a form plurals in -or: blomma becomes blommor.
